questions.title: How do I connect EF Core to PostgreSQL in Docker?
questions.body: I have a .NET service running in a container and a Postgres container on the same network. Every connection attempt times out even though both containers are up. What's the correct connection string when both are Dockerized?

answers.body: That timeout is almost always the hostname - inside Docker you must use the service name from docker-compose.yml as the host, never localhost or 127.0.0.1, since each container has its own network namespace. Double check the Server= value in your connection string matches the Postgres service name exactly.

Also worth checking that you are not publishing the Postgres port and then connecting to the published host port from inside another container - the published port only exists on the host's network namespace, so container-to-container traffic must use the internal port 5432 instead.

questions.title: GraphQL federation with Apollo Gateway returns null for a subgraph field
questions.body: I've set up Apollo Gateway to federate two subgraphs. One subgraph resolves fine, the other always returns null for a field that clearly has data when queried directly. What am I missing in the federation directives?

answers.body: Check that both subgraphs expose the @key directive on the shared entity type and that the routing_url actually resolves from inside the gateway's network - a subgraph reachable from your host but not from the gateway container will silently return null for federated fields instead of erroring.

One more thing to rule out: if the entity's reference resolver is missing on the owning subgraph, the gateway has no way to fetch the rest of the entity and every non-key field comes back null. Make sure ResolveReferenceWith (or its equivalent) is wired up for that type.

questions.title: Kafka consumer group not receiving messages after restart
questions.body: After restarting my consumer, it no longer picks up new messages on the topic even though the producer is confirmed publishing. The consumer group shows as active. How do I debug offset commits going wrong here?

answers.body: This is usually a stale consumer offset combined with auto.offset.reset=latest - if the consumer group was inactive past the topic's retention window its offsets get cleaned up, and on restart it seeks to the tail instead of the last committed offset. Try auto.offset.reset=earliest for local dev.

questions.title: Keycloak client_credentials grant returns invalid_client
questions.body: I configured a confidential client with service accounts enabled, but requesting a token via client_credentials always returns invalid_client. The client ID and secret look correct. What settings am I missing?

answers.body: invalid_client on a confidential client almost always means serviceAccountsEnabled is off, or the client secret sent doesn't match what's stored. Re-check Keycloak Admin Console under the client's Credentials tab, and make sure you're not accidentally sending the client_id twice.

questions.title: Best way to cache with negative caching in Redis using .NET?
questions.body: I want to cache both hits and misses (negative caching) for a lookup that's expensive on miss. What's a clean pattern in .NET with StackExchange.Redis for storing a sentinel value for not-found results?

answers.body: You could just store an empty string for the missing case and treat it as a tombstone on read, though you have to be careful that an empty string is never a legitimate cached value for your data.

Set a really short TTL on everything and the misses take care of themselves eventually - you do not strictly need a separate sentinel value if the expensive lookup is not that expensive to repeat now and then.

questions.title: How to expose multiple ports from one Kubernetes service?
questions.body: My deployment listens on both a REST port and a gRPC port. I want a single Service object routing to both. Is that possible, or do I need two Service resources?

answers.body: A single Kubernetes Service can expose multiple ports - just list them all under spec.ports with distinct name and port/targetPort pairs. Clients then address the same Service DNS name on whichever port they need; you don't need separate Service objects unless you need different selectors.

Note that once you list more than one port, the name field on each entry stops being optional - Kubernetes rejects a multi-port Service where the entries are unnamed, which is a surprisingly common cause of a confusing validation error here.

If the two protocols need different load balancing behaviour or different annotations later on, splitting them into two Services can still be worth it even though one Service technically works fine for the simple case.

questions.title: PostgreSQL migration script fails with duplicate key on re-run
questions.body: Running the same EF Core migration script twice fails on a duplicate primary key. I expected migrations to be idempotent. What's the correct way to make a manual SQL seed idempotent?

answers.body: Manual SQL seeds need an explicit idempotency guard since plain INSERT has none by default - either add a unique constraint and use ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, or wrap the insert in a WHERE NOT EXISTS subquery if there's no natural unique column to conflict on.

questions.title: Difference between routing_url and subgraph_url in Apollo Federation compose config
questions.body: In supergraph.yaml I can specify both routing_url and a separate schema.subgraph_url. What's the actual difference, and when would they point to different hosts?

answers.body: routing_url is where the gateway sends runtime queries at request time; subgraph_url is only used by rover supergraph compose to introspect the schema when building the supergraph. They're often the same address, but need to differ whenever the composer runs somewhere that can't reach the same hostname the gateway uses at runtime.

questions.title: docker-compose external network created by another compose file not found
questions.body: I have one compose file that creates a network and another that references it as external: true. Running the second file alone fails with 'network not found'. What's the right startup order?

answers.body: Compose files with external: true never create the network themselves - whichever file is supposed to create it must be brought up first with a plain non-external network definition. Order your startup scripts so the network-owning compose file runs before anything referencing it.

questions.title: How does MassTransit retry outbox messages after a Kafka broker restart?
questions.body: My outbox pattern publishes via MassTransit to Kafka. When the broker briefly goes down, are in-flight outbox messages retried automatically, or do I need my own retry/backoff policy on top?

answers.body: MassTransit's retry policies apply to consumer-side failures, not outbox publishing - the outbox pattern writes to Postgres in the same transaction as the business change, and a separate background job publishes from that table with its own configurable backoff schedule.

questions.title: Keycloak realm import via --import-realm silently skips a client
questions.body: I'm importing a realm JSON with kc.sh start --import-realm. One client from the export never appears in the admin console after import, and there is no error in the logs. What would cause a client to be silently dropped?

answers.body: A client failing to import silently is almost always a duplicate clientId conflicting with a built-in client, or a validation failure on one of its protocol mappers that Keycloak logs at DEBUG level rather than WARN - re-run with --verbose and grep the log for that client's ID.

questions.title: Redis requirepass connection string format for StackExchange.Redis
questions.body: My Redis container requires a password via --requirepass. What's the correct connection string format to pass host, port, and password together for StackExchange.Redis?

answers.body: The standard format is host:port,password=yourpassword, for example localhost:6379,password=redis_password. You can also add abortConnect=false for local dev so the app doesn't crash if Redis isn't up yet when your process starts.
